deep.reconstruction:
The page is a classification sketch. Grothendieck lists the 'crucial' (cruciaux) types of 1-dimensional arrangements of N >= 4 pseudolines in the projective plane. He says the cases N = 3 are well studied. The criterion he would use to pick these types out is not stated on the page.

The organising notion is the 'ps. droite bigonale'. The reading that fits every case is: a pseudoline that carries exactly 2 vertices of the arrangement, so it is cut into 2 edges. The list splits on whether such a line exists.

1) A bigonal pseudoline exists.
- I_N: a pencil of concurrent pseudolines plus one transversal (the near-pencil). Every pencil line carries only the centre and its meeting point with the transversal, so it is bigonal. The bigonal lines are therefore many (number of pencil lines >= 3).
- I_pq: two pencils of p and q concurrent pseudolines (p >= q >= 2), with centres A and B, plus the pseudoline through A and B. Here N = p+q+1. The vertices are A, B and the pq crossings, so pq+2 vertices. The line AB is the unique bigonal line, since each pencil line carries 1+q or 1+p >= 3 vertices.

2) No bigonal pseudoline exists. The margin examples are N >= 5.
- II_pq: two pencils of p and q concurrent pseudolines without the line AB. Here p >= q >= 2 and N = p+q >= 5, with pq+2 vertices. The bound p+q >= 5 is needed because II_22 is just the simple arrangement of 4 lines, which is listed separately as II_4. The 'minimal' case is p = 3, q = 2 (N = 5, 8 vertices), which he singles out.
- II_4: the simple arrangement of 4 pseudolines, with 6 vertices.
- II_5: the simple arrangement of 5 pseudolines, with 10 vertices.

The margin sketches show the near-pencil, the two-pencil-plus-joining-line configuration, and the two-pencil configuration. A final sentence about the cases without a bigonal line was crossed out.

The list looks like the start of a classification of 'irreducible' or 'minimal non-trivial' pseudoline arrangements. Plausibly these are configurations every non-pencil arrangement must contain, or which serve as building blocks for the combinatorial study of the space of arrangements. This fits Grothendieck's post-1981 interest in pseudoline arrangements as 2-dimensional cell structures related to the Esquisse's Lego/Teichmüller ideas. The page does not state that criterion, and nothing is proved.
errors: Vertex count for I_N is inconsistent with the label 'n = N-1 pseudolines in the pencil'. If N is the total number of lines (N-1 concurrent plus 1 transversal), the projective near-pencil has N vertices, not N+1. N+1 is right only if N denotes the number of pencil lines. The I_pq and II_pq counts (pq+2, with N = p+q+1 and N = p+q respectively) are consistent.
II_4 is the special case II_22 (p = q = 2), which explains the restriction p+q >= 5 in II_pq. The line describing II_4 is crossed out but the label remains, so the list is still in flux.
The defining property of 'crucial' cases is never stated. Completeness of the list (e.g. that every relevant arrangement reduces to or contains one of these) is neither claimed explicitly nor proved.

missed.claim: Grothendieck starts a classification of 'crucial' pseudoline arrangements for N >= 4, using whether a bigonal pseudoline exists and whether it is unique. The governing criterion and the proof of completeness are left implicit or unfinished. This is a structural program of his pseudoline notes, but the families themselves are standard.
missed.quote: Cas cruciaux d'arrangements 1-dimensionnels de ps. droites, avec N≥4 ... 1°) Cas où il existe une ps. droite bigonale ... 2°) Il n'existe pas de ps. droite bigonale
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of mainly historical interest for reconstructing Grothendieck's program on pseudoline arrangements. The configurations listed are well known in combinatorial geometry.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean taxonomy of standard small arrangements: near-pencil, two-pencil configurations, and simple arrangements of 4 and 5 lines. The organising notion of a bigonal line and the label 'crucial' are Grothendieck's own framing. Nothing here appears to be a new result unknown to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Margin vertex counts belong to the case labels: 'N+1 sommets' (I_N), 'pq+2 sommets' (I_pq and II_pq), '6 sommets' (II_4), '10 sommets' (II_5).
Under I_N the parenthesis more plausibly reads '(cas où il existe plusieurs ps. droites bigonales, non unique)'. In the near-pencil all pencil lines are bigonal.
Under I_pq, '(Cas de 6 ps. droites bigonales uniques)' more plausibly reads '(Cas de la ps. droite bigonale unique)'. The line AB is the unique bigonal line.
The I_pq line should read 'plus une ps. droite passant par les sommets des deux faisceaux'.
In II_pq the condition reads 'p≥q≥2, p+q = N ≥ 5'. The crossed-out text after N≥3 near the top is likely 'totalement' or similar, ending '(... étant [?] et bien étudiés)'.
II_4: the text 'Arrangement simple de 4 ps. droites' (with a variant '4 ps. droites en position générale') is crossed out, consistent with II_4 = II_22.
